title: Eucalyptus and spearmint soy candle
subtitle: A clean, minty soy wax jar candle
excerpt: A clean, sharp soy wax jar candle fragranced with eucalyptus and spearmint essential oils at 8% of wax weight. Eucalyptus gives a cool, fresh top note; spearmint softens it with a sweeter mint character. Pour into a 200 ml glass jar and cure for five to seven days before lighting.
sourceNotes: Eucalyptus essential oil (Eucalyptus globulus) flash point: approximately 49°C, below the recommended 65°C pour temperature. Spearmint essential oil flash point: approximately 74°C. Due to eucalyptus's low flash point, add fragrance when wax is at 55°C (not the standard 65°C), and confirm with the supplier SDS. New Directions Aromatics supplier SDS (2022) recommends adding eucalyptus EO below 55°C for candle use. Combined EO load at 8% maintains safe throw without exceeding the wick's capacity.

recipe.batchNotes: Pour multiple jars from a single melt. Add the eucalyptus oil at 55°C, not the standard 65°C.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cure five to seven days before the first burn. Eucalyptus is a top note and dissipates faster than resinous base notes; cure improves throw.
recipe.temperatureNote: Add essential oils at 55°C. Eucalyptus has a low flash point (~49°C); adding it at the standard 65°C pour temperature risks volatilising the essential oil before the wax sets.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a cool, dry cupboard. Eucalyptus and spearmint are top notes and fade faster than base-note fragrances, expect noticeable fading after 12 months.

glossaryTerms.definition: The temperature at which an essential oil can ignite if exposed to a flame. Eucalyptus essential oil has a flash point of approximately 49°C, low for a candle oil. Adding it below 55°C reduces the risk of the volatile components evaporating before the wax sets.
The first burn of a jar candle. Burn until the melt pool reaches the jar edge before extinguishing to prevent tunnelling on subsequent burns.
The resting period after pouring. Top-note essential oils like eucalyptus and spearmint benefit from a full seven-day cure to bind into the wax before the first burn.

content.text: Eucalyptus and spearmint is a clean, sharp soy wax jar candle fragranced with eucalyptus and spearmint essential oils at 8% of wax weight. Eucalyptus gives a cool, fresh top note; spearmint adds a sweeter, gentler mint character. Pour into a 200 ml glass jar and
cure
for five to seven days before lighting.
Add the essential oils at 55°C, eucalyptus has a low
flash point
(~49°C) and the volatile top notes evaporate if the wax is too warm.
Ingredients

items.prepNote: 6% of wax weight; add when wax is at 55°C, not 65°C
2% of wax weight; spearmint has a higher flash point than eucalyptus; add together at 55°C
cotton wick for a 60 to 70 mm jar

content.text: Method
Prepare the jar and wick
Warm the jar briefly, stick the wick tab to the base, and hold with the centring bar.
Melt, cool, add essential oils, and pour

Melt the soy wax to 75°C. Cool to 55°C, lower than a standard soy pour. Add both essential oils and stir for 30 seconds. Pour into the jar immediately at 55°C. The wax may look slightly more opaque than a higher-temperature pour, this is fine.
Cure
Trim the wick to 6 mm after 24 hours. Cure for five to seven days before the first burn.
First burn
The
memory burn
: burn for three to four hours until the melt pool reaches the jar edge. Trim the wick to 6 mm before each subsequent burn.
Shelf life
Two years in a cool, dry place. Eucalyptus and spearmint are top notes that fade faster than base notes, expect noticeable fading after 12 months. Keep the lid on between uses.
